crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Early signals of dementia are subtle changes in memory, language, movement, or behavior that appear before a formal diagnosis. In neuroinformatics, AI models look for patterns in brain imaging, cognitive tests, speech, gait, and blood or spinal fluid biomarkers. The goal is risk stratification and earlier referral, not a standalone diagnosis. This topic sits within The AI Physician, where the site tracks 1000 medical AI models across many specialties.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run on clinical data infrastructure that already exists in hospitals and research centers. That includes picture archiving systems for MRI and PET, electronic health records, speech and sensor recordings, and biobank data. Compute is often cloud based or on secure local clusters with graphics processors for model training. Standards such as DICOM for imaging and FHIR for clinical data help move information between systems. Federated learning is sometimes used so that patient data stays at each site while models are trained across sites.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work usually starts with a curated cohort of patients who have been followed over time, so that labels for conversion to dementia are known. Models then learn from combinations of imaging, genetics, cognitive scores, and digital markers such as typing or speech. Common approaches include convolutional neural networks for scans, recurrent or transformer models for sequences, and survival analysis for time to event. Validation is critical, with internal cross validation followed by external testing on separate populations. The output is typically a risk score or a probability, which a clinician can interpret alongside other findings.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance matters because a model's training data, version, and performance across subgroups must be traceable. Privacy rules such as HIPAA and GDPR shape how identifiable health data can be used, and de identification is not always enough for brain images. Risks include biased performance across age, sex, ethnicity, and education levels, plus the harm of false reassurance or unnecessary anxiety. The site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages and 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, which show that legal exposure is real. Regulatory clearance for clinical use is separate from research validation, and post market monitoring is expected.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward combining blood biomarkers, digital speech and gait measures, and low cost imaging for use in primary care. Research is also exploring multi modal foundation models that can be adapted to smaller datasets. The main barriers are not only technical, they include evidence standards, reimbursement, and equitable access. Progress will depend on prospective trials that show benefit over current practice, not just accuracy on retrospective data. The site tracks 800 scientific models and 732 AI tools, a sign of how quickly the surrounding ecosystem is growing.
